schema.description: Attribution tree via each concept's `topic` field; `edges` holds only prereq edges.

node_fields.name: concept name
node_fields.topic: owning topic id; null for topic nodes
node_fields.default_order: default teaching order within the topic

edge_types.prereq: from must be learned before to; strength=hard|soft

nodes.name: Indices and Surds
nodes.description: Laws of indices for manipulating powers and the simplification and rationalisation of surds, expressing irrational roots in exact form.

nodes.name: Quadratic Functions
nodes.description: Quadratic functions and their parabolic graphs, completing the square to find the vertex, line of symmetry, and maximum or minimum.

nodes.name: Solving Quadratics and Discriminant
nodes.description: Solving quadratic equations by factorising, completing the square, or the formula, with the discriminant determining the number of real roots.

nodes.name: Simultaneous Equations
nodes.description: Solving simultaneous equations, including one linear and one quadratic, by substitution or elimination to find common solutions.

nodes.name: Inequalities
nodes.description: Solving linear and quadratic inequalities algebraically and graphically, and representing the solution sets on a number line.

nodes.name: Functions and Inverses
nodes.description: Functions defined by their domain and range, the distinction between one-to-one and many-to-one mappings, and finding inverse functions.

nodes.name: Composite Functions
nodes.description: Composite functions formed by applying one function to the result of another, with attention to domain and the order of composition.

nodes.name: Modulus Function
nodes.description: The modulus function giving absolute value, its graph, and solving equations and inequalities involving modulus expressions.

nodes.name: Polynomial Division
nodes.description: Dividing polynomials by a linear or quadratic divisor using long division or inspection to obtain a quotient and remainder.

nodes.name: Factor and Remainder Theorem
nodes.description: The factor and remainder theorems relating the value of a polynomial at a point to its factors and to the remainder on division.

nodes.name: Partial Fractions
nodes.description: Decomposing a rational function into a sum of simpler partial fractions, handling linear, repeated, and quadratic factors.

nodes.name: Straight Lines
nodes.description: The equation of a straight line in various forms, with gradient and intercepts found from points or other given conditions.

nodes.name: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
nodes.description: The gradient conditions for parallel and perpendicular lines, where perpendicular gradients multiply to give negative one.

nodes.name: Circles
nodes.description: The equation of a circle from its centre and radius, and finding intersections, tangents, and properties using coordinate geometry.

nodes.name: Arithmetic Series
nodes.description: Arithmetic progressions with a common difference, and the formulae for the nth term and the sum of the first n terms.

nodes.name: Geometric Series
nodes.description: Geometric progressions with a common ratio, formulae for the nth term and sum, and the sum to infinity of a convergent series.

nodes.name: Binomial Expansion (positive integer)
nodes.description: The binomial expansion of an expression raised to a positive integer power using binomial coefficients and Pascal's triangle.

nodes.name: Binomial Expansion (general index)
nodes.description: The binomial expansion for a general rational or negative index as an infinite series, valid within its range of convergence.

nodes.name: Trig Ratios and Graphs
nodes.description: The trigonometric ratios sine, cosine, and tangent, their graphs, periodicity, and exact values for standard angles.

nodes.name: Radian Measure
nodes.description: Radian measure of angles and its use in the arc length and sector area formulae for a circle.

nodes.name: Trig Identities
nodes.description: Fundamental trigonometric identities, including the Pythagorean identities, used to simplify expressions and prove relationships.

nodes.name: Solving Trig Equations
nodes.description: Solving trigonometric equations within a given interval using identities, graphs, and the symmetry of trigonometric functions.

nodes.name: Compound and Double Angle Formulae
nodes.description: Compound-angle and double-angle formulae expanding trigonometric functions of the sum and of multiples of angles.

nodes.name: R-Formula
nodes.description: Expressing a sin θ plus b cos θ in the form R sin(θ + α), used to solve equations and find maxima and minima.

nodes.name: Exponential Functions
nodes.description: Exponential functions and the natural exponential e^x, modelling growth and decay, and the properties of their graphs.

nodes.name: Logarithms and Laws
nodes.description: Logarithms as the inverse of exponentials, and the laws of logarithms for manipulating products, quotients, and powers.

nodes.name: Solving Exponential and Log Equations
nodes.description: Solving exponential and logarithmic equations by applying logarithms and the laws of logarithms to isolate the unknown.

nodes.name: Linearising with Logarithms
nodes.description: Using logarithms to linearise power and exponential relationships, plotting transformed data to determine the model's constants.

nodes.name: Differentiation from First Principles
nodes.description: The derivative defined as the limit of the gradient of a chord, used to differentiate simple functions from first principles.

nodes.name: Power Rule
nodes.description: The power rule for differentiating powers of x, extended by linearity to differentiate sums of polynomial terms.

nodes.name: Chain Rule
nodes.description: The chain rule differentiating a composite function as the product of the derivatives of its outer and inner functions.

nodes.name: Tangents and Normals
nodes.description: Finding the equations of the tangent and normal to a curve at a point, using the derivative as the gradient.

nodes.name: Stationary Points
nodes.description: Locating stationary points where the derivative is zero and classifying them as maxima, minima, or points of inflection.

nodes.name: Connected Rates of Change
nodes.description: Connected rates of change linking the time derivatives of related quantities through the chain rule.

nodes.name: Product and Quotient Rules
nodes.description: The product and quotient rules for differentiating the product and the quotient of two functions.

nodes.name: Derivatives of Special Functions
nodes.description: Differentiating exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions using their standard derivative results.

nodes.name: Implicit Differentiation
nodes.description: Implicit differentiation finding the derivative of a relation not solved explicitly for y by differentiating both sides.

nodes.name: Parametric Differentiation
nodes.description: Parametric differentiation finding dy/dx for curves defined parametrically by applying the chain rule through the parameter.

nodes.name: Indefinite Integration
nodes.description: Indefinite integration as the reverse of differentiation, finding antiderivatives with an arbitrary constant of integration.

nodes.name: Definite Integration and Area
nodes.description: Definite integration evaluating the area under a curve between limits using the fundamental theorem of calculus.

nodes.name: Integration of Standard Functions
nodes.description: Integrating standard functions, including powers, exponentials, and trigonometric functions, from their known antiderivatives.

nodes.name: Integration by Substitution
nodes.description: Integration by substitution reversing the chain rule by changing the variable to simplify the integrand.

nodes.name: Integration by Parts
nodes.description: Integration by parts reversing the product rule to integrate the product of two functions.

nodes.name: Integration using Partial Fractions
nodes.description: Integrating rational functions by first decomposing them into partial fractions that can be integrated individually.

nodes.name: Volumes of Revolution
nodes.description: Volumes of revolution generated by rotating a region about an axis, computed by integrating the area of circular cross-sections.

nodes.name: Locating Roots
nodes.description: Locating roots of an equation by a sign change over an interval, establishing the existence of a root before iteration.

nodes.name: Iterative Methods
nodes.description: Iterative methods finding successive approximations to a root using a rearranged iterative formula, and assessing convergence.

nodes.name: Forming Differential Equations
nodes.description: Forming differential equations from descriptions of rates of change, translating a physical situation into an equation.

nodes.name: Separation of Variables
nodes.description: Solving first-order differential equations by separating the variables and integrating each side.

nodes.name: Vectors in 2D and 3D
nodes.description: Vectors in two and three dimensions represented in component and unit-vector form, with addition and scalar multiplication.

nodes.name: Magnitude and Direction
nodes.description: The magnitude of a vector from its components using Pythagoras, and finding its direction and corresponding unit vector.

nodes.name: Scalar Product
nodes.description: The scalar (dot) product of two vectors, used to find the angle between them and to test for perpendicularity.

nodes.name: Vector Equations of Lines
nodes.description: The vector equation of a line through a point with a given direction, and finding intersections and angles between lines.

nodes.name: Complex Number Arithmetic
nodes.description: Complex numbers in the form a + bi, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and the complex conjugate.

nodes.name: Argand Diagram
nodes.description: Representing complex numbers as points or vectors on an Argand diagram, illustrating their geometric interpretation.

nodes.name: Modulus-Argument Form
nodes.description: The modulus-argument (polar) form of a complex number, with multiplication and division combining moduli and arguments.

nodes.name: Complex Roots and Loci
nodes.description: Complex roots of polynomials occurring in conjugate pairs, and loci in the complex plane defined by modulus and argument conditions.

nodes.name: Kinematics with Constant Acceleration
nodes.description: Kinematics of straight-line motion with constant acceleration, using the suvat equations to relate displacement, velocity, and time.

nodes.name: Variable Acceleration
nodes.description: Kinematics with variable acceleration, using differentiation and integration to relate displacement, velocity, and acceleration over time.

nodes.name: Projectiles
nodes.description: Projectile motion analysed by resolving into independent horizontal and vertical components of motion under gravity.

nodes.name: Forces and Equilibrium
nodes.description: Resolving forces into components and applying the conditions for the equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces.

nodes.name: Friction
nodes.description: The frictional force opposing motion, modelled by the coefficient of friction and limiting equilibrium on a rough surface.

nodes.name: Newton's Laws of Motion
nodes.description: Newton's laws of motion relating the resultant force acting on a body to its mass and resulting acceleration.

nodes.name: Connected Particles
nodes.description: Analysing connected particles, such as those joined by a string over a pulley, by applying Newton's laws to each.

nodes.name: Work, Energy and Power
nodes.description: Work done by a force, kinetic and potential energy, the work-energy principle, and power as the rate of doing work.

nodes.name: Momentum and Impulse
nodes.description: Linear momentum and impulse, and the conservation of momentum applied to collisions between particles.

nodes.name: Representation of Data
nodes.description: Representing data using histograms, box-and-whisker plots, and cumulative frequency graphs to display its distribution.

nodes.name: Central Tendency and Spread
nodes.description: Measures of central tendency and spread, including the mean, median, variance, standard deviation, and quartiles.

nodes.name: Permutations and Combinations
nodes.description: Permutations and combinations counting ordered arrangements and unordered selections of objects.

nodes.name: Probability Rules
nodes.description: The rules of probability, including the addition and multiplication rules for combined, mutually exclusive, and independent events.

nodes.name: Conditional Probability
nodes.description: Conditional probability of an event given another, and the use of tree diagrams with the multiplication rule.

nodes.name: Discrete Random Variables
nodes.description: Discrete random variables with a probability distribution, and the calculation of their expectation and variance.

nodes.name: Binomial Distribution
nodes.description: The binomial distribution modelling the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials with constant probability.

nodes.name: Geometric Distribution
nodes.description: The geometric distribution modelling the number of independent trials up to and including the first success.

nodes.name: Poisson Distribution
nodes.description: The Poisson distribution modelling the number of random events occurring at a constant average rate in a fixed interval.

nodes.name: Normal Distribution
nodes.description: The normal distribution, a continuous bell-shaped distribution defined by its mean and variance, standardised using the z-score.

nodes.name: Normal Approximations
nodes.description: Using the normal distribution to approximate the binomial or Poisson distribution under suitable conditions, with continuity correction.

nodes.name: Sampling
nodes.description: Sampling concepts including populations, samples, and the sampling distribution of the mean used for statistical inference.

nodes.name: Hypothesis Testing
nodes.description: Hypothesis testing using a test statistic and a significance level to decide between a null and an alternative hypothesis.
